candidates.title: Confidence gate adjusted for Choice option count

found.context: Review of the public TypeSafe introduction and linked documentation, checked against this repository's preserved synthetic receipts.

candidates.mechanism: Store each Choice confidence threshold with the option set it was tuned on, convert it to the top probability it requires ((c*(n-1)+1)/n, the inverse of confidence c = (n*p-1)/(n-1)), re-tune when options change, and sum probabilities per downstream action before gating.
candidates.code_owns: Threshold storage and conversion, option-set versioning, per-action probability sums, and the gate decision.
candidates.delta: H11 falls back to a taxonomy parent and H32 audits agreement across repeats; neither normalizes thresholds by option count.
candidates.next_step: Closed; see the controls collection evaluation.
candidates.resolution: Published as CT01 in controls/catalog.json on 2026-09-23 after a four-fixture live screen.

candidates.title: Tool-call trace audit split between code and Jev

found.context: Review of the public TypeSafe introduction and linked documentation, checked against this repository's preserved synthetic receipts.

candidates.mechanism: For an agent tool-call trace, code checks call/result ID binding, argument schemas, exact value equality and cross-call value flow; Jev judges only tool suitability and whether a free-text argument refers to the requested entity.
candidates.jev_judges: Tool suitability per call; entity reference of free-text arguments.
candidates.code_owns: ID binding, schema validation, equality of request fields, arguments and earlier outputs, missing results.
candidates.delta: E23 judges field pairing in one assembled record and L04 selects a handler before a call; neither partitions a multi-call trace.

candidates.title: Compound-request split and re-ask

found.context: Review of the public TypeSafe introduction and linked documentation, checked against this repository's preserved synthetic receipts.

candidates.mechanism: A Noul detects several distinct actions; an LLM splits the request; code caps the split count; Jev checks joint coverage and that nothing was added; each command is re-evaluated by ordinary routing before confirmed execution.
candidates.jev_judges: Compound detection; split coverage; added-action check; per-command routing.
candidates.code_owns: LLM call, split cap, confirmation, execution order and permissions.
candidates.delta: H28 batches independent questions; it neither splits a request nor checks split coverage.
candidates.next_step: Closed; see the controls collection evaluation.
candidates.resolution: Published as CT03 and CT04 in controls/catalog.json on 2026-09-23 after a four-fixture live screen.

candidates.title: Two Choice options overlap

found.context: Building the controls collection: pre-inference review of the human-AI catalog had found nine overlapping contracts by hand, and the duplicate screen's kernel review asked for an insufficient-description outcome.

candidates.mechanism: Code enumerates the option pairs of a Choice contract and asks, one pair per question, whether a realistic input could satisfy both descriptions without a stated precedence; overlapping pairs go back to the author before any fixture is frozen.
candidates.jev_judges: Whether two option descriptions can both apply to one realistic input under the contract's instructions.
candidates.code_owns: Pair enumeration, contract versioning, routing flagged pairs to the author, and the rewrite itself.
candidates.delta: L23 judges primitive fit and L12 instruction applicability; neither inspects two labels of one contract for overlap. Applied to 26 new contracts before their fixtures were written; it prompted precedence sentences in five.
candidates.resolution: Published as CT08 in controls/catalog.json on 2026-09-23 after a four-fixture live screen.

candidates.title: Capability-claim audit with a partial outcome

found.context: Phase 0 source audit of two public open-source repositories: a cross-check, blind to the analysts' verdicts, of 23 capability claims from a design brief against source-cited findings.

candidates.mechanism: Remove the analyst's verdict labels from a claim-check table and give Jev only neutral, source-cited findings. Ask one supports/insufficient/contradicts question per atomic capability claim. Code compares Jev's choices with the analyst's SUPPORTED/PARTIAL/NOT FOUND verdicts and sends disagreements and low-confidence splits back for review. A three-way Choice has no partial outcome, so author each broad capability claim as two sub-claims (the capability exists; it meets the stated bar) or add an explicit partially_supports option.
candidates.jev_judges: Whether the supplied findings support, contradict, or are insufficient for each atomic capability claim.
candidates.code_owns: Claim atomization, removal of analyst verdicts from the evidence, source citation and retrieval, comparison with the analyst table, the review threshold, and the final verdict.
evidence: Binding: result.json is the complete response-bearing receipt from jev-1.13.0 (23 check answers with probabilities). Its request_sha256 60f52090ea78a00130a405159e7e8029105f0f563affd25dd41f594b1a699afd reproduces from request.json by rebuilding the jev-workflows check body (the evidence as state, one fixed supports/contradicts/insufficient Choice per claim) and hashing its canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8). Its evidence_sha256 78d0ef33b14c34dbba30d0306792de86c4f02fee92bcfad2e7897d33b26d8fa8 equals the SHA-256 of the evidence text in request.json. File SHA-256: request.json e49b9f64ed39755a579fd51c06fd7e1909b91f0d3c1bfd5caed2f05e722394d0, result.json ddf478e8241fb59c5f3f664df3d0a3432186be82aee54ec6df9327c2ba5ec594

Observed in result.json: Jev agreed with all 16 analyst SUPPORTED verdicts; of 7 analyst PARTIAL or overstated verdicts, 3 strictly worded claims came back contradicts at confidence 0.97 or higher, 3 came back as low-confidence splits (top confidence 0.11 to 0.44), and 1 loosely worded claim came back supports at 1.0
Limitation: one run, one domain, and claim wording was authored by the same harness that held the analyst verdicts
candidates.delta: H37 checks whether located context supports one claim, and E22 whether evidence supports one field. This applies the check to a table of broad capability claims whose truth is often partial, blind to the analyst's own verdicts. It shows that a three-way outcome turns partial truth into a low-confidence split, a confident contradiction, or a confident support, depending on claim wording.
candidates.next_step: Write a contract with a partially_supports option (or existence and adequacy sub-claim pairs), freeze fixtures from public repositories with analyst verdicts held outside provider inputs, and screen it live against the three-way version.

candidates.title: New validator invariant against the producer's reachable output

found.context: Code-review triage of a change that added one invariant to a record validator (a count of automatic moves must not exceed a count of agreed moves) in a local toy game.

candidates.mechanism: When a change adds an invariant to a validator, ask whether any genuine producer path can emit a record that violates it. Supply the producer, the new invariant, and the upstream rule that is supposed to guarantee it, because the guarantee often lives in a different function. Code then runs the producer across its modes (a property run) and stored records through the new validator.
candidates.jev_judges: Whether the supplied producer and upstream rules show a reachable output that violates the new invariant, show a guarantee that prevents it, or are insufficient.
candidates.code_owns: Choosing the invariant and producer, assembling the guarantee chain, the property run over producer modes, re-validating stored records, and the final verdict.
evidence: Receipt digest only (private project code is not published): request_sha256 f915fe5a6e3dd3bf3679bf8a5f9631019a8d3054e941da307d95d13da52f8c06

Observed: with the upstream guarantee given only as a one-line summary, the three-way Choice split 0.39 no-defect, 0.37 defect, 0.24 insufficient (confidence 0.09); twelve sibling questions in the same request answered at 0.56 to 0.99.
Observed: exact checks refuted the lead; 40 randomized producer runs across every mode, plus 10 two-sided runs, all produced records that passed the new invariant.

Synthetic example: a refund validator newly requires refunded_total <= captured_total; the refund writer caps each refund at the remaining captured amount in a separate helper. Without that helper in the packet, the question cannot be settled.
Limitation: one run and one domain; the split may reflect the packet omitting the guarantee rather than a general property.
candidates.delta: BH12 asks whether a migration removes a field that a supported old reader still needs. This runs the other way: the reader gains a rule, and the question is whether current or stored writer output can break it. It also records a packet requirement: include the upstream guarantee itself, not a summary of it.
candidates.next_step: Write a contract with the guarantee chain as a required state field, freeze synthetic fixtures (guarantee present, guarantee absent, genuine violation), and screen whether including the guarantee turns the split into a confident answer.
